In the #GreatLakes, Pink and Chinook salmon can hybridize to create a hybrid called a "pinook” First found in the early 1990s in the St. Marys River, pinooks have variable characteristics and their appearance can be similar to either parent species #25DaysofFishmas doi.org/10.1016/j.jg...

The #GreatLakes pink salmon population was the first known to complete its entire life cycle in freshwater and has the only known occurrences of fish living to be 3 years old instead of 2, possibly because of slow growth rates due to the lakes’ relatively low-nutrient, cold waters #25DaysofFishmas

Pink salmon wouldn’t be out of place at the North Pole! 🎅 They're a cold water species native to the North Pacific Ocean extending from Siberia to Alaska, and down the west coast of North America. They’ve also been unintentionally introduced to the #GreatLakes + parts of Europe #25DaysofFishmas

Unlike Coho + Chinook salmon intentionally brought to the #GreatLakes for recreational fishing, pink salmon were unintentionally introduced in the 1950s to Lake Superior (exact cause uncertain: nas.er.usgs.gov/queries/Fact...), but since then, populations have been self-sustaining #25DaysofFishmas

Establishment of pink salmon in the Great Lakes was mentioned by Elton in Ecology of Invasions. This prompted Bev Scott to inform Elton of attempts to introduce Pacific salmon in other locations (see letter below, from the Elton archives at Oxford; cited in the 2020 edition of Ecology of Invasions]
